title: Reprocessing: replay retained raw observations under newer normalizers
description:
Design and implement a first-class reprocessing contract: a normalization attempt is identified by (source report/payload digest, adapter/normalizer identity+version, schema version, execution time). Reprocessing preserves the original raw observation and original normalized interpretation, producing a NEW derived interpretation rather than rewriting history; idempotent replay of the same payload under the same versions creates no duplicate facts; disagreement between old and new normalized outputs is explicit; reprocessing is offline (never contacts the provider); malformed historical payloads fail retentively and can succeed under a later parser version; bounded batch planning answers 'which retained observations would change under normalizer version N' before committing. Acceptance case: retained provider payloads whose fields were raw-only gain typed facts from a newer normalizer without network access or destruction of the older interpretation.

## Context
From GitHub issue #8 (filed by maintainer 2026-10-07). Repeated catch-up beads (unp/o6y/8jj/cyp) marked gaps reprocess-able from retained raw, but no reprocessing path exists - the benefit is still an implementation detail.
acceptance_criteria: OpenSpec change; reprocess identity/versioning contract; offline replay proven with a real retained-raw example; idempotency + history-preservation tests; batch planning surface; gates green.
notes: Completed 2026-10-08: OpenSpec change add-reprocessing-contract (archived, specs synced). remote_sync/reprocess.py: read-only bounded plan (retained raws with run linkage, stale adapter version vs replay adapter, already-reprocessed skips via deterministic 64-hex origin digest = sha256(reprocess:raw:adapter:schema) - origin references are hash-formatted by record contract); execute replays reconstructed envelopes offline (zero requests, reprocess-origin runs via migration 0014 extending the origin-kind vocabulary trigger + records/common frozenset), shared page writer commits, payload never touched, observation-digest dedup, malformed retained payloads fail retentively (failed run + diagnostic, retryable). CLI catalog reprocess plan|run (danbooru/aibooru/gelbooru/e621) with mock-transport adapters that assert if contacted. VERSION DISCIPLINE ESTABLISHED: all four providers bumped to -v2 (this week's normalizer changes had shipped unversioned - a real contract gap the bead exposed); fixture manifests aligned + guard test. LIVE: 6 danbooru raws replayed complete (31-41 records each), re-run skipped, 6 zero-request reprocess runs, no observation explosion. OUT OF SCOPE (documented): run-less raws (lookup responses, import raws) - no operation linkage; pixiv offline replay (auth-gated constructor) can follow if needed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Materialize-a-seed: non-recorded item entry point with full evidence bundle
description:
Implement the decided materialize-a-seed operation: an explicit operator command that creates a provenance-marked stub post (operator-asserted observation, availability unknown, no snapshots) from the full evidence bundle present at the time. Interface takes, in decreasing trust: (1) innate image metadata preferred - local bytes through the existing hashing/inspection machinery (verified sha256/md5, detected mime, dimensions, versioned phash) at verified status; (2) supplied-alongside references - URLs, provider-declared hashes, dimensions, platform IDs - recorded at declared or operator-asserted status with source; (3) the seed assertion event itself. Stub then seeds every lookup strategy like any recorded post; cross-catalog matching runs against existing items; later real observations upsert enrichment; asserted-only stubs stay distinguishable in queries.

## Context
Decided with maintainer 2026-10-05 (bead data-processing-zos; design recorded in docs/plans/cross-platform-media-catalog.md section 12 'Non-recorded item entry'). Requirement 1 of docs/plans/raw_requirements.md covers items both recorded and non-recorded; today lookup seeds must be existing catalog entities.
acceptance_criteria: OpenSpec change + spec requirements; materialize CLI surface with private-input redaction; stub posts carry operator-asserted provenance and availability unknown; verified-hash/dimension facts from local bytes; declared/asserted references normalized through existing typed-reference machinery; stub is a valid lookup seed for external_post_id and hash strategies (regression test); idempotent re-materialize; full gates green.
notes:
Phase 1 completed 2026-10-06 (autonomous session): OpenSpec change add-materialize-seed implemented - SeedMaterializationService (src/media_catalog/seeding/) + 'catalog seed create' CLI. Bundle (urls+note+declared_md5) retained as raw operator_seed import evidence; stub post availability=unknown with primary canonical URL; every URL attached as source_url link + typed provider_id reference under the seed's raw observation; idempotent (digest-matched complete run reused); fail-closed on empty/unrecognized/handle-only/conflicting-per-platform URLs and malformed note/md5; creates no candidates/relations/decisions; stub verified as external_post_id lookup seed (planning test). 10 tests in tests/test_seeding.py; docs in media-catalog guide + audit bridge finding 6 updated. REMAINING (phase 2, next session): local-bytes intake - hash a held file through the existing inspection machinery into verified asset facts (likely via the adoption/CAS path with an operator-designated root; decide integration), declared-md5 occurrence linkage on the stub, and closing the OpenSpec change once phase 2 lands (change stays unarchived until the bead completes).
Phase 2 (local-bytes intake) completed 2026-10-07; bead COMPLETE. --file validation (regular file, inspection byte ceiling, sha256+md5 streamed) with the content hash in the bundle digest (changed bytes = new seed); declared MD5 verified against the bytes BEFORE any write (adoption's own exact verification remains the second gate); media occurrence on the stub (source_key operator-seed, declared_md5, local_path) registered as legacy_local occurrence source under an operator-seed managed source root (sha256-of-parent identity, matches adoption's candidate query); _ensure_adopted runs after commit only when no asset is linked yet -> adopt_assets into --media-root, fingerprint read from detected_* columns + asset_fingerprints phash row (assets.width/phash are the legacy x-likes surface). title: Link discovery GC deletes sync-created external links and aborts the run (FK failure)
description: Why: probing the bookmark-to-database pipeline (2026-10-05), after syncing one danbooru post (whose declared source_url wrote a post_external_references row referencing external_links id 6363), catalog discover-links fails with FOREIGN KEY constraint failed. DiscoveryService.discover's end-of-run garbage collection (src/media_catalog/discovery/__init__.py ~99-115) deletes external_links rows that lack link_observations and external_link_references, but external_links has two more legitimate attach points it ignores: post_external_references (written by metadata sync for declared source URLs) and account_external_links. A sync-created link therefore looks like garbage to the GC, its deletion is blocked by the FK, and the entire discovery run aborts - breaking the offline workflow for any catalog that has synced metadata. What needs to be done: widen the GC predicate so a link is deletable only when nothing references it (no link_observations, no external_link_references, no post_external_references, no account_external_links); add a regression test that seeds a sync-style post_external_reference on an observation-less link and asserts discovery completes and the link survives.
close_reason: Closed

title: e621 candidate lookup rejects the e621 response envelope (malformed_response on every result)

Evidence retained in catalog-output/catalog.sqlite3 as candidate lookup run 4 and its raw observation payload. What needs to be done: teach the e621 lookup response parser the {posts: [...]} envelope (the e621 metadata adapter already parses this shape for post sync), add a fixture test covering both empty and non-empty e621 lookup responses, and re-run the probe seed to confirm outcome success with result_count 0.

title: Export projections: bounded JSONL/CSV views over the evidence layer
description: Why: the 2026-10-04 gap analysis against docs/plans/raw_future_plan.md found the catalog CLI has no export surface at all (search/stats/inspection only), making the projection layer the other half of the distance to the plan's described functioning ('then projection is cheap'). All underlying evidence — raw observations, declared vs verified facts, attribution evidence per source — is already retained, so export projections are the highest-leverage non-Phase-D work toward the plan. This is the roadmap's Operations and portability thread. What needs to be done: (1) bounded JSONL/CSV export projections intended for analysis and migration, with explicitly stated projection policies — offline by default, and no private paths, credentials, cookies, signed URLs, or raw payloads in output; (2) an attribution-disagreement report: cases where two providers disagree on artist attribution, drawn from retained evidence without overriding review decisions; (3) exports carrying which source supplied each field (per-field provenance, richest observation wins per a stated policy while retaining all dissenting values); (4) later, once the Phase D relationship model exists: variant-family exports that group near-duplicates, exclude thumbnails, and prefer upstream originals. The durable database remains the evidence layer; consumer schemas and exports are projections with stated policies.
notes: GitHub design input attached 2026-10-07: gh#6 (projections must be reproducible and auditable, not convenient dumps - projection kind/schema version, db/schema version, selection+ordering policy, relationship/variant and preferred-representation policy, field-source policy, inclusion/exclusion counts with reasons, stable evidence-layer identifiers, generation timestamp + tool version, deterministic digest over the projection spec and exported manifest; sidecar/manifest over embedding provenance in every row). Fold these into the change proposal when this bead starts.

title: Artifact/work entities and typed relationship model (kernel Phase D schema half)
description: Why: the 2026-10-04 gap analysis against docs/plans/raw_future_plan.md shows the evidence backbone (observations, blobs, representations, evidence/review ledgers, storage-enforced immutability) is complete, and this is the missing layer for the plan's five-version functioning — same bytes / re-encode / crop / censored variant / edit as separately observed objects joined by evidence-backed relationships. It is the first schema consumer of the kernel epistemic vocabulary and does NOT depend on the matching research spike (tracked separately in data-processing-8nj); the halves were split on 2026-10-04. What needs to be done: (1) design the artifact/work entity — a conceptual content object that several representations and blobs manifest, designed in kernel terms; (2) one uniform typed-relationship table carrying epistemic status (observed/verified/derived/inferred/reviewed) with relationship types like same_bytes, reencoded_from, resized_from, cropped_from, censored_variant_of, edited_from, thumbnail_of, reposted_from, probably_same_work, confirmed_same_work; (3) seed it with already-deterministic or provider-observed types that need no fuzzy matching: same_bytes from existing SHA-256 dedup, thumbnail_of from occurrence variant roles, reposted_from from provider-declared source URLs; (4) leave fuzzy matcher proposals entering later as inferred candidates through the existing evidence/review ledger; (5) first projections on top, e.g. variant-family grouping that excludes thumbnails and prefers upstream originals. Constraints: new migrations must ship storage-level immutability from their first migration per the kernel spec; matching never auto-confirms identity, authorship, or same-work; keep media vocabulary (dimensions, codec, format) in the media family layer — file extension/MIME is an attribute (declared media_occurrences.mime_type vs verified assets.detected_mime_type), usable as relationship evidence, never the relationship itself; no data migration of existing tables.
notes: GitHub design inputs attached 2026-10-07: gh#2 (artifact/work identity boundaries - settle work vs representation layering, edit/censorship/crop semantics, multipage/video modeling, grouping concepts vs same-work/variant relations, directional vs symmetric kinds, deterministic vs inferred conclusions; deliverable: semantic decision table with concrete fixture examples BEFORE the first generic relationship migration) and gh#3 (relationship evidence/review lifecycle independent of candidate matching - conclusion-row vs evolving-epistemic-state design, history preservation, multi-evidence bundles, review reversal, detector/version placement, deterministic bypass, canonical orientation; deliverable: lifecycle state diagram + storage invariants). Both are design requirements for this bead, not separate work items.

title: Add bounded Gelbooru metadata adapter
description: Create and implement the add-gelbooru-metadata-adapter OpenSpec. Support two explicit metadata transports: credentialed JSON DAPI and anonymous HTML for individually requested posts. title: Evidence dependence and lineage: mirrored sources are not independent corroboration
description:
Distinguish observation count from independent corroboration count: define how source/repost/derivation relationships express that an assertion or occurrence likely descends from another source; decide whether evidence rows need an optional lineage/group/correlation reference or dependence derives from the source/relationship graph; preserve uncertainty - dependence itself may be observed, derived, inferred, or reviewed. Design doc first; interacts with t08 relationship typing and the evidence ledger (provenance-kernel spec); future confidence/projection logic must not over-count copied claims.

## Context
From GitHub issue #9 (maintainer, 2026-10-07). As cross-source relationships improve, the same claim repeats across mirrors (pixiv -> danbooru -> gelbooru -> archives); observation count must not be confused with independent-corroboration count. Same for byte-identical files across five providers: five occurrences, one origin assertion.
acceptance_criteria: Design decisions recorded (lineage reference vs derived dependence); evidence-row semantics specified; kernel/evidence spec updated if adopted; a worked example over the pixiv->danbooru->gelbooru mirror chain.

title: Temporal/as-of knowledge as a deliberate evidence-layer capability
description:
Design 'what was known when': distinguish observed_at, provider-reported timestamps, acquisition time, normalization/reprocessing time, and review time; as_of policy for projections without rewriting history; timelines for deleted/moved/renamed/corrected objects; review-state and relationship-conclusion reconstruction as of a cutoff; exports record their evidence cutoff. Guardrail: no event-sourcing framework for its own sake - exploit retained history and make temporal semantics explicit before projections assume latest-only. Likely delivers a design doc + kernel-spec requirement first; surfaces (as-of queries, change reports between cutoffs, disagreement reports) follow.

## Context
From GitHub issue #7 (maintainer, 2026-10-07). The repo already retains append-only source reports, provenance-event revisions, immutable run inputs, and review history - the ingredients for temporal queries exist but the capability is unnamed and undesigned.
acceptance_criteria: Design document with timestamp-taxonomy decisions; kernel spec requirement if adopted; at least one as_of-capable surface demonstrated over real retained history.

Keep exact hashes and pHash, evaluate established-library alternatives before inventing anything custom, record per-class distributions/FP/FN rather than picking a global threshold. Extends scripts/matching-spike/ and the evidence document.

The spike evidence (docs/plans/matching-spike-evidence.md) flags same_artist_near_negative with ZERO samples - the measured pHash separation may be optimistic. title: Local mirror vs live API strategy for provider metadata at scale
description: Why: the user flagged that target-database metadata can reach tens to hundreds of millions of rows - keeping local copies to work against, fetching against APIs, or both depending on where data is needed has different costs: storage, slowness, API communication, and provider etiquette. This decision shapes every audit-driven capability (matching by hash or source needs queryable provider metadata). What needs to be done: (1) size the realistic metadata footprint per provider and per use (full dumps exist for some boorus; others only offer paged APIs); (2) define which queries must be local (offline joins, hash indexes, dedup sweeps) vs which can stay bounded live lookups; (3) evaluate options: no mirror + live lookup only, partial selective mirror (per-artist work corpora), full metadata mirror with periodic refresh, or external bulk datasets; (4) write the decision into the catalog plan with its performance and efficiency rationale, honoring the repo principles (offline by default, bounded network, projections over the evidence layer).

title: Supervised matching research spike (kernel Phase D research half)

Split from the original Phase D bead on 2026-10-04: the artifact/work and typed-relationship schema lands separately as data-processing-t08 and does not depend on this spike; conversely this spike does not block the schema work. Lower priority because it is only needed before fuzzy matchers, not before relationships exist. What needs to be done: curate a fixture set of real originals, recompressions, mirrors, and crops from the already-synced catalog; measure which signals (exact SHA-256/MD5, provider-declared vs verified hashes, perceptual hashes at multiple sizes/thresholds, aspect ratio and dimensions, chronology, source links) actually separate the classes; document distance distributions and false-positive rates; compare approaches used by czkawka-style duplicate finders per the roadmap research section, including resize and recompression robustness, crop-aware or region-based matching, and false positives among visually similar but unrelated artwork. No metric or threshold automatically establishes artist identity, authorship, same-work, source direction, or preferred quality — those conclusions require provenance and review.
notes: Session analysis 2026-10-04: this issue bundles two separable halves. (1) Schema half — artifact/work entities + the uniform typed-relationship table; seedable without any fuzzy matching via already-deterministic or provider-observed types: same_bytes (existing SHA-256 dedup), thumbnail_of (variant roles), reposted_from (source URLs). (2) Research spike — required only before matchers propose probably_same_work/inferred types. The halves can land separately. Extension/format facts are attributes (media_occurrences.mime_type declared vs assets.detected_mime_type verified), usable as evidence for reencoded_from/transcoded_from; detected-MIME vs URL-extension mismatch is cheap reviewer-facing evidence.

title: Decide multi-size perceptual hash storage

What needs to be done: if a concrete metadata consumer needs finer fingerprints, decide whether phash@16 is stored as a new fingerprint kind (migration plus FINGERPRINT_KINDS change) or a new algorithm version, per the kernel no-speculative-schema guardrail.
